# Threat Model — Cars JO (Jordanian Car Marketplace)

## Overview
White-box assessment of a Next.js 16 (custom `server.js`, Socket.io) marketplace app at `/workspace/Cars-JO` ("Cars JO" / jo-cars-marketplace), Prisma 5 ORM with SQLite dev DB (`prisma/dev.db`), next-auth JWT + custom `src/lib/auth.ts`, Cloudinary uploads, OpenAI integrations (`src/app/api/ai/*`), admin panel under `/admin` and `src/app/api/admin/**`. Also ships Expo mobile app (`CarsJOApp/`) consuming the same API. Product surfaces: `src/`, `server.js`, `prisma/schema.prisma`. Non-product: `lumek_dark_sector/` (GameMaker project), `*.apk`, `backups/`, PDFs, k6 test scripts, `.next/`, `node_modules/`.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
- **Unauthenticated attacker**: can reach all `GET` public APIs, auth/register, contact, some AI endpoints. Geo-block middleware exists but sandbox/local traffic is unaffected.
- **Registered user (low priv)**: can post cars, comments, forum posts, messages, bookings, tickets, upload images. Must not read/modify other users' data (IDOR risk), must not reach `/api/admin/**` (BFLA risk).
- **Dealer/trader roles**: approved via admin; elevated posting rights.
- **Admin**: full access via `user.role === 'ADMIN'` checks in each route — inconsistent enforcement is a primary risk.
- **Attacker-controlled input**: all request bodies/query params, uploaded files (multer/Cloudinary), AI chat messages, JWT payloads, socket.io events.
- **Trusted**: server env, prisma client,.Cloudinary/OpenAI upstreams.

## Attack Surface
169 API routes. Key areas: `api/auth/*`, `api/admin/*` (~50 routes), `api/cars/*`, `api/users/*`, `api/messages|conversations`, `api/upload`, `api/ai/*` (LLM), `api/admin/backup` (file ops), forum/comments (XSS), auctions/payments-like flows (business logic, race conditions), socket.io real-time layer, `server.js` custom server.

## Severity Calibration
- **Critical**: unauth RCE, auth bypass / JWT forgery, admin-route access as non-admin, mass user PII dump, SQL injection to data theft.
- **High**: IDOR exposing/modifying other users' data at scale, stored XSS in listings/comments, file upload leading to code exec, privilege escalation via mass assignment, SSRF via scrape/AI.
- **Medium**: XSS requiring interaction, missing rate limits on auth, info leaks aiding attack.
- **Low**: header/config hygiene, enumeration without demonstrated impact.
